item.title: Octavus Regulatory Updates - Jun 2026 to Sep 2026
item.description: US and EU approvals, recalls and policy updates, including FDA draft guidance for genome-editing therapies, the PreCheck manufacturing pilot, the FDA rule on non-animal methods and EMA's voluntary NAM data submission pilot.

Data.lnsights.Decisions. RECALLS EU Based Recalls This slide is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Jun 02, 2026 Company Name: Becton Dickinson Product: ChloraPrep 2% w/v / 70% v/v cutaneous solution 1mL applicators Reason: Potential breach of sterility in the packaging process Indication: Fast-acting antiseptic skin preparation Jul 09, 2026 Company Name: Bristol Laboratories Product: Phenoxymethylpenicillin 250 mg/5 ml Oral Solution Sugar Free Reason: Product labelling issues Indication: Mild to moderately severe bacterial infections Note: We have covered recalls irrespective of drug category Aug 20, 2026 Company Name: Zentiva Pharma Product: Fingolimod Zentiva 0.5 mg Capsules Reason: Potential risk of contamination with metal particles Indication: Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis Jul 13, 2026 Company Name: Becton Dickinson Product: ChloraPrep 2% w/v / 70% v/v cutaneous solution 1mL applicators Reason: Potential breach of sterility in the packaging process Indication: Fast-acting antiseptic skin preparation 5

Data.lnsights.Decisions. UPDATES US Based Updates This slide is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Jun 02, 2026FDA Releases Draft Guidance to Fast ‑ Track Cell and Gene Therapies FDA issued draft guidance enabling genome-editing gene-therapy developers to leverage public and platform knowledge, including CMC, nonclinical, and clinical data, to streamline submissions. Sponsors must justify applicability, maintain safety and efficacy standards, engage FDA early, and submit comments within 90 days. Jun 29, 2026FDA selects seven firms for a drug manufacturing pilot FDA selected seven companies for its PreCheck Pilot Program to strengthen US pharmaceutical manufacturing and supply-chain resilience: Amneal, Cellares, Eli Lilly, FUJIFILM Biotechnologies, Kriya Therapeutics, Kyowa Kirin, and Regeneron. The two-phase model offers early facility guidance and enhanced application support. Sep 21, 2026 FDA revises regulations to promote innovative alternatives to animal testing FDA rule: Clarifies that Non-Animal Methods (NAMs) can support safety assessments of drugs and biologics before human trials, where appropriate Expanded approaches: Recognizes human cells, organ-on-chip systems, and computational models, while replacing animal-focused terminology with “nonclinical” No new requirements: The rule does not prohibit animal studies, change evidentiary standards, or add new development requirements NAMs database & comments: FDA launched a 25-example NAMs use-case database and is accepting public comments; significant adverse comments could lead to withdrawal and standard rulemaking 6

UPDATES EU Based Updates This slide is non-exhaustive. For additional details or clarifications, please feel free to contact us at bd@octavusconsulting.com Jul 02, 2026 EMA advances efforts to address women’s health needs Sep 01, 2026 Voluntary Data Submission Pilot to Accelerate Alternatives to Animal Testing EMA launched a voluntary data submission pilot to facilitate the sharing and regulatory assessment of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including organoids, microphysiological systems, and computational models Purpose: Support the replacement or reduction of animal studies in medicines development Submission & feedback: Companies, researchers, and other stakeholders can submit NAM data independently of marketing applications and receive non-binding expert feedback Regulatory impact: The pilot aims to build regulatory experience, harmonise assessment approaches, and strengthen NAM acceptance across Europe Timeline: Submissions are expected through Q3 2027, followed by an EMA lessons-learned report Women’s health focus: EMA is integrating sex-specific considerations across medicines development and regulation Clinical & safety assessment: Focus includes trial representation, efficacy, safety, dosing, and pregnancy/breastfeeding evidence, alongside pharmacovigilance Evidence generation: EMA will expand DARWIN EU® real-world evidence studies, identify research gaps, and reduce regulatory uncertainty Collaboration & priorities: EMA will strengthen stakeholder and international collaboration, with the 28–29 September Women’s Health Workshop helping shape future priorities Data.lnsights.Decisions. 7
